newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rise as investors buy favorites.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rise as investors buy favorites.

text.p: Stocks rose Thursday as investors continued to buy shares of Wall Street's favourite companies after Christmas.

Shortly after 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 27.29 at 6,550.14, boosted by rises in International Business Machines Corp. and AT&T Corp. The gains put the Dow above its record close of 6,547.79 set on Nov. 25.
In the broader market, gainers outpaced losers by 14 to seven on light volume of about 146 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"There is a time-honoured game in force -- the mutual funds go in and start buying up their favourite names that were strong during the year, like Cisco, Microsoft and 3Com," said James Cramer, president of Cramer Co. "They need to advertise winners."
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks of large companies led the major market indexes on a percentage gain basis, rising 4.02 points, or 0.54 percent to 755.05.
"We're seeing a follow-through from the Santa Claus rally we had on Tuesday," said Alan Ackerman, senior vice president and market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
"The market is finishing the year with a bang," Ackerman said. "Records were made to be broken, and we continue to break records. We've had Christmas in Wall Street nearly every month of 1996."
The Nasdaq Composite, heavily weighted with technology companies, rose 4.54 points to 1,292.17.
Microsoft Corp. rose 7/8 to 85-3/4 and touched a new year high of 86-1/8. Cisco Systems Inc. rose 1-9/16 to 66-9/16, and Intel Corp. rose 1-3/8 to 136-7/8. Trading was very heavy in all three stocks.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose 2/32, reducing the yield to 6.58 percent from 6.59 percent at Tuesday's close.

Long distance companies jumped after the Federal Communications Commission proposed to cut the $23 billion paid in access fees by long-distance companies to local service providers. AT&T shares rose 1-1/4 to 42-3/4 in heavy trading. WorldCom Inc. gained 7/8 to 24-7/8 and MFS Communications Co. Inc. gained 1-1/2 to 51-3/4.

A statement from General Electric Co., stating that it was not interested in buying American Express Co., calmed Wall Street's recent buyout speculation between the firms. American Express shares fell 1-5/8 to 57-1/2, losing some of their gains fuelled by the rumours.
"These are seasonally very strong days for the market. It's just going to be like this for the next few days," Cramer said.
